stories.title: Salesforce Acquires Cresta for ~$2.7B, Adding Voice AI Agents to Service Cloud
stories.body: On November 2, 2026, Salesforce signed a definitive agreement to acquire Cresta, a voice-first AI platform, for a reported $2.7 billion — its third CX acquisition in two weeks after completing the $3.6B Fin (formerly Intercom) pickup. Cresta's platform runs customer calls end-to-end and provides real-time guidance to human reps; named enterprise customers include Marriott, Comcast, and Alaska Airlines. After closing, Cresta will continue to support the third-party contact center and telephony platforms its customers already use, though analysts warn to watch whether new capabilities land first on Service Cloud Voice.
stories.why: Cresta is now a Salesforce asset — any retail or CPG prospect running a Salesforce CRM stack will be steered toward Agentforce + Cresta as a bundled voice-agent suite, shrinking the independent vendor landscape. Sellers should use this consolidation to show prospects why a neutral, composable context layer (not a CRM-locked agent) preserves flexibility as the market folds in on itself.

stories.title: Sierra Raises $1.75B at $30B Valuation as Annual Revenue Passes $400M
stories.body: On November 23, 2026, Sierra — the enterprise customer-service agent company co-founded by Bret Taylor — announced a $1.75B Series F led by Greenoaks and Lightspeed, nearly doubling its May 2026 valuation of $15.8B. The company reports annual recurring revenue passed $400M in October 2026, roughly two and a half years after launch, and says it now serves close to 50% of Fortune 50 firms. Sierra's outcome-based pricing model — charging only when agents deliver a resolution — is a key differentiator it is using to defend against Salesforce's Agentforce and the newly acquired Fin.
stories.why: Sierra's $30B valuation on $400M ARR sets a market-price anchor for outcome-based enterprise AI agents that every retail CIO will reference in vendor negotiations. Retail sellers competing against or alongside Sierra need to understand its 'Ghostwriter' build-and-improve loop and explain where a context/data layer they don't provide is the gap that makes or breaks agent accuracy.

stories.title: Neo4j Launches Context Engine to Create a Shared Knowledge Layer for Enterprise AI Agents
stories.body: On October 20, 2026, Neo4j announced the Neo4j Context Engine, a product that lets companies rapidly build a reusable, shared knowledge substrate — including a predefined six-layer Business Ontology — that multiple AI agents can consistently reason over. The engine includes graph-native memory so agents learn from past decisions, and decision-tracking logs that create a permanent record of agent reasoning. The launch directly targets the most common enterprise AI failure mode: agents hallucinating or contradicting each other because they draw from siloed, stale data rather than a single governed context.
stories.why: This is the architecture story a retail AI seller needs on every discovery call: Neo4j is now a named, shipping product that gives enterprises the shared context layer without which agents in ordering, service, or supply chain will conflict and fail. Use it to frame the question — 'what is your shared knowledge layer?' — before proposing any agent workflow.

stories.title: McKinsey State of AI 2026: 32% of Enterprises Cancelled a Software Purchase to Build With Agents Instead — But ROI Stays Flat
stories.body: McKinsey's 'The State of AI in 2026: On the Road to ROI,' published August 25, 2026 from a survey of 1,719 respondents across 97 countries, found that 32% of organizations decided against buying at least one software product or feature because they could build it in-house using agentic coding tools — rising to nearly half among AI high performers. Among large enterprises (revenue >$1B), 40% now report scaling AI agents in at least one function, up from 27% the prior year. Despite this activity surge, the share of respondents reporting any EBIT impact from AI stayed flat at 37%, and McKinsey's own summary states: 'Organizations' conviction in AI is growing faster than the immediate financial returns they can attribute to it.'
stories.why: The 32% build-vs-buy signal is the objection retail CIOs will raise on every vendor call in Q1 2027 — sellers must be ready to quantify run-cost, maintenance burden, and the hidden cost of building without a governed data foundation. The flat ROI finding is equally powerful: it explains why pilots stall and positions a pre-built, context-grounded agent layer as the faster path to measurable return.

stories.title: Forrester Mid-2026: Most 'Agentic' Retail Experiences Are Still Conversational; Gartner Warns 40% of Agent Projects Will Fail by 2027
stories.body: Forrester's mid-2026 assessment states bluntly that most so-called agentic commerce experiences today remain conversational — humans still drive decisions and checkout in the vast majority of cases — and advises enterprises to build a 'machine advantage' through structured, AI-readable product data on infrastructure they control. Separately, Gartner predicts that more than 40% of agentic projects will fail by 2027 because legacy systems cannot support modern AI demands, and that 60% of large enterprises running agents in production will face external accountability requirements for autonomous actions by 2030. Gartner also expects 90% of B2B buying to run through AI agents by 2028, pushing over $15 trillion through agent exchanges.
stories.why: The Forrester/Gartner one-two punch — agents are mostly still chat today, but legacy data architecture is what kills the projects that try to go further — is the exact narrative that justifies a context-layer investment before scaling agents in ordering or supply chain. Retail sellers can cite these named analyst findings to validate urgency while explaining why the data foundation must come first.
